full_source_text_analysis.explanation: The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in Torah #271. The text consists of exactly three sentences and uses exclusively causal language: 'עַל יְדֵי' (through/by means of), 'מֵחֲמַת' (because of), and 'תָּלוּי בָּזֶה' (depends on this). All concepts in the teaching — עַזּוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה (holy boldness), דִּבּוּר עִם הָרַב (speaking with the teacher), עֲבוֹדַת ה' (divine service), הִתְעוֹרְרוּת (spiritual awakening), and קֵרוּב (closeness to the Rebbe) — are connected by causal eitza chains only, not by bechina (shared-nature) relationships.

eitza_chain_summary.from: עֲבוֹדָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה וְעוֹבֵד הַרְבֵּה אֶת ה'

full_source_text_analysis.structural_note: The teaching describes a virtuous feedback loop: עֲבוֹדָה → עַזּוּת → דִּבּוּר עִם הָרַב → הִתְעוֹרְרוּת → עֲבוֹדָה. Each arrow is a causal eitza, not a bechina equivalence. The Rebbe explicitly states that each element 'starts from the other' (כָּל אֶחָד מַתְחִיל מֵחֲבֵרוֹ) and 'depends on this' (זֶה תָּלוּי בָּזֶה), which is circular causation, not shared essence. This is the defining feature that confirms eitza, not bechina, for every edge in this Torah.
